_meta.title: Plugins deliberately NOT in ai-kit catalog
_meta.notes: ai-kit's catalog is for COMPLEMENTARY tools, not ALTERNATIVES that overlap ai-kit's own integrated skills. During initial design (gstack, gsd, superpowers, mattpocock-skills, etc were studied), the best ideas were distilled INTO ai-kit's lifecycle. Recommending these plugins alongside ai-kit creates double-bundle noise. The audit emits KEEP-EXTERNAL with the reason from this file instead of ADOPT, so users see deliberate non-adoption (not 'promotion candidate').

excluded.name: superpowers
excluded.reason: Meta-skill bundle (obra/superpowers-marketplace). Overlaps with ai-kit's /ai:tdd, /ai:review, /ai:retro, /ai:ship, /ai:plan-* and others — best patterns were distilled into ai-kit's own lifecycle during initial design. Adding it as a recommended plugin would create double-bundle noise.

excluded.name: taste-skill
excluded.reason: Anti-slop frontend design pack (Leonxlnx/taste-skill, installs via `npx skills add` — not a Claude Code marketplace plugin, so it does not fit the plugins.json schema). Overlaps the existing design entries (frontend-design / lazyweb) and ui-ux-pro-max; single-source preview. Its distinctive value (GSAP motion code skeletons + AI image-board generation) is design *generation*, out of scope for what ai-kit recommends as durable per-project infra. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: If a project specifically wants its motion/image-board generation, install directly: `npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill`. Use ui-ux-pro-max for reasoned design-system output.

excluded.name: designlang
excluded.reason: Live-DOM design-system EXTRACTION tool (Manavarya09/design-extract, npm `designlang`). Ships an MCP server + Claude Code plugin, so it is structurally eligible for the mcp-servers.json bucket — but it optimizes none of the AI-loop dimensions the companion catalog is for (graphify=input, caveman=output, llm-wiki=memory, context7=docs); it emits frontend artefacts (DTCG tokens / Tailwind / shadcn / Figma) from a URL. That is one-shot task tooling you run when cloning/matching a design, not durable per-project infra that compounds each session. Fails the promotion-quorum bar (single-maintainer, v12.23 high-churn, sponsor-affiliate README → 1 source, preview-only, never default-recommended). Same out-of-scope bucket as taste-skill (design generation/extraction). should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: If a frontend project genuinely needs live-site token extraction or CI drift-check against a deployed source-of-truth, install directly and wire its MCP: `npx designlang <url>` / `designlang mcp`. Use ui-ux-pro-max for reasoned design-system output.

excluded.name: codebase-memory-mcp
excluded.reason: Code-intelligence MCP server (DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp, pure-C static binary, MIT). Builds a persistent knowledge graph via tree-sitter (158 langs) + 'Hybrid LSP' type resolution; 14 MCP tools (search_graph, trace_path, Cypher query_graph, semantic search, cross-service HTTP linking). Structurally eligible for the mcp-servers.json bucket, but it is an ALTERNATIVE to graphify (ai-kit's knowledge-graph/input companion, wired into CLAUDE.md + query workflow + PreToolUse hook) — not complementary. Its own README says it is 'similar in spirit to graphify's graphify-out/'. Two knowledge-graph tools = double-bundle noise. Adopting it also runs against ADR-0006 (ai-kit deliberately dropped MCP; stays pure Bash+Markdown, minimal footprint) and its curl|bash install auto-wires config + hooks across 11 agents. Fails promotion-quorum like designlang/taste-skill: single org, README = sole source. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Whether it should REPLACE graphify (stronger engine on paper) is a separate deliberate spike, not a catalog add — tracked in #109.
excluded.alternative: Keep graphify as the knowledge-graph companion. If a project specifically wants type-aware call graphs / semantic / Cypher search, install directly and wire its MCP per the upstream README. Migration decision: see issue #109.

excluded.name: headroom
excluded.reason: Context-compression layer for AI agents (headroomlabs-ai/headroom, Apache-2.0, ~47k stars, active). Proxy + MCP + library that compresses tool-outputs/logs/RAG/files 60-95% before the LLM, plus an output-shaper (verbosity steering + effort routing). In-category (token efficiency) and popular — NOT wrong-category like the design tools — but Ignored as a blanket companion on three grounds: (1) footprint vs ADR-0006 — Python 3.10+ + HuggingFace model (Kompress-v2-base) + optional pytorch-mps + long-running proxy, against ai-kit's pure-Bash+Markdown / MCP-dropped / minimal posture; (2) trust surface — the proxy sits in the path of all prompts+responses, exchanges provider/Copilot OAuth tokens, and `headroom learn` auto-edits CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (the files ai-kit's own loops own); lossy pre-agent compression is a correctness gamble vs ai-kit's verifiability ethos; (3) dimension-spanning overlap — its output-shaper dubbelt caveman, its cross-agent memory/learn dubbelt llm-wiki + the checkpoint loop. Only its proxy tool-output compression is genuinely new (graphify indexes code, not a 65k-token log). should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Whether that one novel angle earns a 'runtime-output' companion entry is a separate deliberate spike, not a catalog add — tracked in #110.
excluded.alternative: Keep graphify (code input) + caveman (output) as the orthogonal companions. If a specific project drowns in large runtime tool-outputs (SRE logs, big grep/RAG dumps) AND accepts the proxy trust surface, install directly and wire its MCP per upstream: `pip install headroom-ai[all]` / `headroom mcp install`. Adoption decision: see issue #110.

excluded.name: skillspector
excluded.reason: Security scanner for AI agent skills (NVIDIA/SkillSpector, Apache-2.0, Python 3.12+). 68 vuln patterns across 17 categories (prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, supply chain, MCP tool poisoning, …), two-stage static + optional-LLM, SARIF/JSON/MD output, scans repo/URL/zip/dir/file. Ships a CLI + an MCP server (`scan_skill`), so structurally eligible for the mcp-servers.json bucket — but it is one-shot scanner tooling, NOT a per-session compounding companion like the catalog is for (graphify=input, caveman=output, llm-wiki=memory, context7=docs). Footprint (Python + optional-LLM API spend + MCP/long-running scan) runs against ADR-0006 (pure Bash+Markdown, MCP-dropped, no runtime daemon), same posture objection as headroom/codebase-memory-mcp. So it does NOT belong as a recommend-to-everyone companion. UNLIKE the prior Ignores it is neither wrong-category (taste-skill/designlang) nor a duplicate-of-existing-companion (codebase-memory-mcp/headroom): it plugs a real hole in ai-kit's OWN trust machinery — VETTING.md's seven criteria have no automated security/malicious-pattern dimension, yet ai-kit emits 27 skills + recommends 12 plugins under an implicit 'safe to wire' endorsement. NVIDIA-backed + Apache-2.0 clears the single-maintainer/license quorum concerns that sank the others. should-i-use verdict: Ignore (catalog) / Wire-as-internal-tool. Whether to wire `skillspector scan --no-llm` (static, zero-API) as an advisory CI gate on ai-kit's emitted skills + a probe step in should-i-use/recommend-rules is a deliberate spike, not a catalog add — tracked in #111.
excluded.alternative: Don't add to the companion catalog. If wiring as ai-kit's own security gate proves out (#111), it lives in CI + the vetting pipeline, not in a recommend-to-everyone table. To scan a single skill ad-hoc today: `uvx --from git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector skillspector scan <dir> --no-llm` or via the bundled `scan_skill` MCP tool.

excluded.name: openspec
excluded.reason: Spec-driven planning framework for AI coding agents (Fission-AI/OpenSpec, npm `@fission-ai/openspec`, MIT, Node 20.19+, no MCP / no API keys). `openspec init` creates an `openspec/` tree (changes/<feature>/{proposal,design,tasks}.md + specs/ + archive/) and wires `/opsx:explore|propose|apply|verify|archive` into 30+ agents. Same bucket as `superpowers`: an ALTERNATIVE lifecycle, not a complementary companion. Every stage already has an ai-kit equivalent — explore=grill-me/grill-with-docs, propose=to-prd, tasks=to-issues, apply=tdd+review, archive=ship+retro, design.md=docs/adr/*, cross-session persistence=checkpoint/resume+roadmap.md, specs/=CONTEXT.md+GH issue body. Wiring it forks the command namespace (/ai:* vs /opsx:*) and the contract surface (GH issue with DoR/DoD gates vs openspec/changes/*/tasks.md), and `openspec init` auto-edits AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md — the files ai-kit's own loops own (same objection as headroom). Footprint (global npm + Node) is a mild ADR-0006 hit but not disqualifying on its own; the category overlap is. Promotion-quorum not assessed — single org, README as sole source — because the category rejection is dispositive. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Its one genuinely novel idea — the requirement delta as an in-repo artifact reviewable in the same PR as the code, where ai-kit's contract surface is deliberately the GH issue body — is a deliberate spike against ai-kit's OWN lifecycle, not a catalog add: tracked in #112.
excluded.alternative: Use ai-kit's own lifecycle skills (grill-with-docs → to-prd → to-issues → tdd → review → ship). If a project specifically wants in-repo spec folders, install directly: `npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest && openspec init` — but do not run it alongside ai-kit's planning skills. Spec-delta-in-diff question: see issue #112.

excluded.name: openwiki
excluded.reason: Agent-written repo documentation CLI (langchain-ai/openwiki, npm `openwiki`, MIT, TypeScript, built on LangChain DeepAgents; 10.4k stars, v0.1.1). An LLM agent reads the repo, writes prose docs into `openwiki/`, appends a pointer block to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, and keeps itself current off `git log <last-head>..HEAD --name-status` on a scheduled CI job that opens a PR. Two modes: code mode (repo docs) and personal mode (raw sources → wiki, with Gmail/Slack/Notion/X/Tavily connectors). Ignored on category, NOT on trust — LangChain org + MIT + real release clears the single-maintainer/license quorum that sank designlang/taste-skill. Grounds: (1) double overlap — code mode is an ALTERNATIVE to graphify (incl. its `--wiki` tier at graphify-out/wiki/), personal mode is an ALTERNATIVE to llm-wiki (same Karpathy lineage ai-kit already vendored its own schema for); wiring it makes a third `wiki` surface next to the two that already need companions.json's 'Two wikis present — disambiguation' block. (2) For code, it is a strict downgrade vs graphify: LLM-generated prose bakes hallucination to disk and costs API spend per update, where graphify is AST-derived (deterministic, zero cost, incremental via `graphify update .`). (3) ADR-0006 footprint — global npm + Node + DeepAgents runtime + per-update API spend; and it auto-edits AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, the files ai-kit's own loops own (same objection as headroom and openspec). should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Its one genuinely reusable idea — anchoring a generated artifact to a git head so staleness is COMPUTABLE instead of hoped-for — needed no adoption: graphify already stamps `built_at_commit` into graph.json, and ai-kit now reads it in the docs-sync `graph-fresh` check (v1.47.0), which caught a 34-file/3-commit stale graph in ai-kit itself on first run.
excluded.alternative: Keep graphify (code, AST-derived) + llm-wiki (non-code documents) as the two wiki-shaped companions. Staleness detection ships in `/ai:docs-sync` → graph-fresh (`bin/ai-kit-docs-sync-graph-fresh.sh`); the fix is `graphify update .`, AST-only and free. If a project genuinely wants LLM-written architecture prose with a CI PR gate, install directly per upstream — but do not point it at a repo that already has graphify, and review every generated page before an agent treats it as truth.

excluded.name: ponytail
excluded.reason: Always-on 'lazy senior dev' ruleset (DietrichGebert/ponytail, MIT, JS plugin, ~89k stars, active). A YAGNI ladder injected every turn (exists?→reuse→stdlib→native→dep→one-line→minimum) that biases the agent toward the smallest code while never cutting trust-boundary validation, error handling, security, or accessibility; ships for ~20 hosts (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, …) plus /ponytail-review|audit|debt commands. In-category (NOT wrong-category like the design tools) and well-evidenced, but Ignored as REDUNDANT: its entire job — write only what the task needs, don't over-build — is already ai-kit's own `pre-write-discipline.mini.md` (universal, always-on, shipped this repo) reinforced by the LEAN feedback rules; and caveman (already a companion) covers the orthogonal comms-compression half that ponytail explicitly leaves alone (its own FAQ: 'use both'). Wiring ponytail would run a SECOND always-on 'write less' ruleset next to pre-write-discipline — double-injection every turn, a second source of truth for one rule, drift risk — which LOWERS cohesion. Replacing caveman with it (the user's question) is a double loss: caveman's value is comms compression, which ponytail does not do. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Its one genuinely novel contribution — a reproducible agentic benchmark proving the discipline measurably cuts ~54% LOC without dropping a safety guard — is adopted-as-pattern (the measurement insight, not the code): whether/how to measure pre-write-discipline within ADR-0002's deterministic zero-cost constraints is a deliberate spike, tracked in #119.
excluded.alternative: Keep `pre-write-discipline.mini.md` (universal, always-on) + the LEAN feedback rules as the minimal-code discipline, and caveman for comms compression. Do NOT replace caveman with ponytail — orthogonal jobs. If a project specifically wants ponytail's plugin, install upstream: `/plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail` then `/plugin install ponytail@ponytail` — but not alongside pre-write-discipline. Measurement question: see issue #119.

excluded.name: technical-writing
excluded.reason: Layered technical-writing skill (pasted SKILL.md, no upstream repo, no licence stated). Stacks four layers: Diataxis document modes, Google developer style, ASD-STE100 instruction rules, and Global English syntax. Three of the four duplicate what ai-kit already ships: the Google, STE and Global English layers restate `writing-style.mini.md` and /ai:copywriter's 39 patterns, down to identical examples (use not utilize, help not facilitate). It also delegates its slop catalogue to an `unslop` skill that does not exist here, and carries `disable-model-invocation: true`, so as a skill it never fires on its own. should-i-use verdict: Ignore as a whole. Its one non-redundant layer, Diataxis, was adopted as a pattern instead: `standards/rules/docs-diataxis.mini.md` (2026-08-20), ~45 lines, on-demand, crediting diataxis.fr.
excluded.alternative: Use `docs-diataxis.mini.md` for document structure, `writing-style.mini.md` for the always-on sentence floor, and /ai:copywriter for the full editor. Do not install the skill alongside them.

excluded.name: unslop
excluded.reason: 31-pattern AI-tell editor (pasted SKILL.md, no upstream repo, no licence stated), marked 'must always apply'. Already inside ai-kit by two routes, so adopting it a third time would triple one source. Patterns 1 to 25 share the same lineage as /ai:copywriter's §1-33, namely Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing. Patterns 14, 26, 27, 28, 30 and 31 are the source of `writing-style.mini.md` rules 1 to 6 and of copywriter §34-39: the same jargon list (substrate, wedge, north star, flywheel), the same plain-word list (utilize, facilitate, numerous), and the same mechanism-over-feeling example. Both surfaces now credit it. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Nothing in it is missing from ai-kit.
excluded.alternative: Use `writing-style.mini.md` (always-on floor) and /ai:copywriter (full 39-pattern editor). Both name unslop in their provenance sections; update those if the upstream list changes.

excluded.name: kakashi
excluded.reason: Local-first PII/secret masker CLI + agent rule (Muhammadatef/kakashi @ 49d51d1cc2044561cfd0771e277e12f69636be1d, MIT, npm @muhammadatef/kakashi 1.0.0). Ignore, on four independent grounds. (1) Wrong control layer: it installs a markdown rule asking the agent to run `kakashi scan` before pasting, but the agent has already read the file into context by then and cannot un-see it; its own README concedes that an @-mention leaks the full body on that turn. Advisory-where-enforcement-is-needed fails open exactly when it matters. ai-kit already catalogs the enforcing version in hooks-patterns.json: `gitleaks-scan` and `block-env-edits`, both PreToolUse/Edit|Write, which the model cannot talk itself out of, plus secrets-hygiene.mini.md prescribing gitleaks pre-commit + CI. (2) Marketing/code parity fails on the headline claim: it advertises .env, but getFormat() keys off path.extname(), which returns '' for `.env` and `.envrc` and '.local'/'.production' for `.env.local`/`.env.production`. Every real dotfile form errors 'Unsupported file format'; only `something.env` works. Verified against this repo's own context/templates/repo/.envrc and tests/fixtures/audit-laravel-*/.env.production. (3) Precision is too low to mask with: the full_name pattern is /\b[A-Z][a-z]+(\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+\b/ (any TitleCase bigram, matched across newlines), cc is \b\d{13,19}\b, hex_secret is 40+ hex chars. On a 6-line sample doc it returned 7 findings of which 2 were real: 'React Native', 'Release Notes\nBuilt' and 'See Design System' masked as [FULL_NAME_n], a 13-digit epoch-ms timestamp as [CC_1], a pinned git SHA as [HEX_SECRET_1]. Scanning this repo's own standards/rules/secrets-hygiene.mini.md masks 'Secrets Manager' as [FULL_NAME_1]. Credential regexes (db_conn, env_secret, bearer, provider key prefixes) are competent; the PII half is not. (4) Cost and scope: install.sh hardcodes --all, so curl|bash appends a 73-line always-on block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, writes ~/.cursor/rules/kakashi.mdc with alwaysApply:true, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.windsurf/rules/, mutates ~/.continue/config.json systemMessage, and copies 6 slash commands per agent -- a machine-wide, every-session context tax for a person-scoped concern, which is the shape /ai:dedupe and the context-lean check in /ai:hygiene exist to flag. Also `npm audit`: 2 high, xlsx@0.18.5 prototype-pollution + ReDoS with no fix available (SheetJS left npm) -- a parser aimed at untrusted spreadsheets is the wrong place for that. Maturity: 20 stars, 8 commits, 1 fork, 0 issues, single release 2026-06-04. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: For the enforcement this actually promises, wire the `gitleaks-scan` and `block-env-edits` PreToolUse hooks from hooks-patterns.json via /ai:recommend-tools, and follow secrets-hygiene.mini.md (gitleaks pre-commit + CI, rotate on suspicion). For a genuine one-off need to hand a spreadsheet or PDF to an LLM with names and IDs stripped, run it ad hoc -- `npx -y github:Muhammadatef/kakashi mask <file>` -- read the diff before sharing, and wire nothing.
